3 Compaction

A percussion corer compresses sediment: you recover a shorter core than the hole you made. Correcting for it restores the original depths — and must leave the carbon unchanged, because the tube holds exactly what came out of the ground. The depths stretch by the compaction factor and the bulk density thins by the same factor, so the two cancel.

Core Compaction factor In-situ depth (cm)
WWF-01-A 1.121 65
WWF-01-B 1.111 30
WWF-01-C 1.143 72
WWF-01-D 1.137 58
WWF-01-E 1.094 35
WWF-01-F 1.083 26

4 Putting cores on common depths

Cores reach different depths and were sliced at different thicknesses, so they are splined onto standard intervals with a mass-preserving spline (mpspline2). Below the base of a core the profile is modelled, not measured, using an asymptotic curve with a non-zero recalcitrant floor.

Every interval records how much of it is measured rather than modelled, and stocks are apportioned by that fraction — so a core ending at 26 cm contributes only its real 4% to the 25–50 cm interval.

The deep figure is reported to 50 cm, the deepest depth every core supports. Cores that went deeper are not credited for it; that is the price of one comparable number.

5 The estimate

Each stratum’s mean is weighted by its area, not by how many cores landed in it, using a design-based stratified estimator (survey) with a finite population correction.

Stratum Mean 0-25 cm (kg C/m²) SE
Seagrass / eelgrass 2.00 0.41
Salt marsh 5.17 0.25

The interval rests on 4 degrees of freedom. With this few cores it is wide, and no amount of analysis narrows it — only more cores, or a looser target, will.

6 Combining with what was already known

The planning stage used a prior to size the campaign. That prior is still true afterwards, so it is used again here as evidence — a weighted average, where each source contributes in proportion to its precision.

The prior comes from 82 Zostera marina cores across 11 estuaries in the Janousek et al. (2025) synthesis, filtered to sites that resemble this one and excluding this site’s own cores, which appear in that synthesis and would otherwise be counted twice.

Source Mg C/ha Weight
Prior (sites like this one) 21.7 ± 7.9 11%
Evidence (these cores) 31.4 ± 2.7 89%
Posterior (combined) 30.4 ± 2.6 —

The prior earned 11% of the weight. Most of the answer comes from the fieldwork, which is what a campaign of this size should produce.

7 What to be careful about

  • The deep number is partly modelled. Below each core’s base the profile is an extrapolation, and the per-core modelled share is in the table above.
  • 4 degrees of freedom is very few. The confidence interval is honest but wide, and the between-stratum comparison has low power — a non-significant result there is not evidence the strata are equal.
  • Stratum areas drive the site total. They come from STRATUM_AREAS_M2 in 00_config.R; if those are placeholders, so is the total.
  • The prior assumes independence. It excludes this site’s own cores. If you move this workflow to another meadow, check PRIOR_EXCLUDE_ESTUARY again.
  • No map here. Mapping where the carbon sits needs far more cores than this — see 06_advanced_spatial.R.

8 Methods

Step Method Source
Compaction Depth stretch with matching bulk-density correction from scratch — matches the digital data sheet
Depth harmonization Mass-preserving (equal-area) spline mpspline2 — Bishop et al. (1999); Malone et al. (2009)
Below-core profile Asymptotic model with a non-zero recalcitrant floor base stats SSasymp — shape after Kindeberg et al. (2019)
Stratified estimation Design-based stratified mean with finite population correction survey — Lumley (2004, 2010); Cochran (1977)
Prior Similarity-matched subset of a regional core synthesis Janousek et al. (2025), figshare 28127486
Combination Normal-Normal precision-weighted update from scratch — Gelman et al. (2013) §2.5
